headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Flowise can write shared files while gpt-researcher reads/writes research artifacts and sends them to external APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can write to the server filesystem and gpt-researcher reads local documents and uses browser/API tools, so attacker-controlled content can cross from one agent to the other through shared files. The pathway is plausible in default deployments, though not proven to be automatic. Both agents expose file-based I/O surfaces.
conditions: IF Flowise writes untrusted content into a shared workspace that gpt-researcher later ingests as a document or prompt.
IF gpt-researcher treats retrieved file content as instructions rather than data.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files.
Add a manual review step before gpt-researcher consumes Flowise outputs.
Prefix all inter-agent files with a machine-readable data schema.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and content filtering at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, and gpt-researcher processes local documents while sending queries and reports through broad network egress to third-party APIs. If they share files or a datastore, sensitive content can flow from Flowise into gpt-researcher and then out to external services. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default configurations.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace, datastore, or uploaded files.
IF Flowise outputs contain secrets or sensitive chatflow inputs.
IF gpt-researcher forwards those files or excerpts to external APIs.
mitigations: Keep sensitive Flowise outputs out of any shared folder.
Run gpt-researcher with network access disabled for sensitive tasks.
Use separate API keys and principals for each agent.
Review and redact files before research ingestion.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and Flowise explicitly supports shared state via server datastore while gpt-researcher supports multiple instances and subprocesses. That overlap creates a real write-conflict risk on shared artifacts even without git access. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore.
IF concurrent runs modify the same report, prompt, or uploaded file.
IF no external lock or lease mechanism is present.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple manual lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same workspace.
Snapshot inputs before handing them to the second agent.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based orchestration layer that can emit tool outputs, and gpt-researcher has planner/execution/publisher roles that can turn upstream text into reports or actions. If gpt-researcher consumes Flowise output without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into published research. The pairwise pathway is plausible and potentially broad in impact.
conditions: IF Flowise output is passed directly into gpt-researcher as authoritative input.
IF gpt-researcher publishes or summarizes without source verification.
IF downstream consumers rely on the resulting report for decisions.
mitigations: Require source citations before publication.
Insert a verification step between agents.
Mark Flowise output as untrusted input.
Limit gpt-researcher to drafting only.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, while gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and external APIs. The profiles do not specify residency, retention, or certification boundaries, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because uncertainty must escalate, medium is appropriate rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as customer documents or secrets are processed by both agents.
IF one agent stores or logs data longer than the other.
IF data residency or DPA requirements differ between the two services.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs.
Check retention settings for both agents.
Use separate tenants or projects.
Document the data flow before deployment.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and DPA controls across both systems.
